name: gear-knit-scarf-skitter
prompt: The reference image shows a small creature; use it ONLY to judge proportions. Do NOT draw the creature, its body, its outline, or any part of it — the image must contain nothing but a scarf. Draw a cozy knit scarf as ONE very long, very wide, shallow downward-curving band, much wider than it is tall, stretching edge to edge across the frame. CRITICAL GEOMETRY: the band keeps its full sweep all the way out — it does NOT bend, curl, or turn until the outermost tips, and at the very tips each end flips back with a tiny fold, like a ribbon wrapping out of view behind something wide. Plus one short tail hanging from the front-right of the band, ending in yarn fringe tassels. Sticker-flat cel style, every region ONE perfectly even solid color like a vector illustration — no shading variation, no wash, no mottling — one thick confident uniform rounded outline in a darker wine shade of the scarf's own color, never black. The ENTIRE scarf filled with deep muted berry red (#a34b54) — a dark, rich, saturated wine red fill, NOT pink, NOT pastel, NOT white — with soft warm cream (#f2e9d3) for a few flat stitch dashes and the fringe. Scarf centered, spanning nearly the full frame width, on a plain solid magenta (#ff00ff) background, no shadow. Negative constraints: no white fill, no pink, no pastel colors, no gray, no gradients, no texture, no stipple, no halftone, no watercolor, no 3d render, no clay, no cast shadow, no drop shadow, no background scenery, no creature, no body, no dome, no face, no eyes, no legs, no early curl, no inward hook, no outline sketchiness, no black outline, no text, no watermark, no sticker border, no die-cut white edge.
